title: Grateful Dead Live at Danish Center on 1966-03-12
taper: Source disc provided by Terry Doherty

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience tape of a high‑energy 1966 show with standout “One Kind Favor” and the infamous Ice Cream Break, though the mix is uneven.
ai_review.review: The performance captures an early Acid Test era Dead that’s rocking hard, highlighted by Bob Weir’s nascent guitar work on One Kind Favor and Ron “Pig” McKernan’s vibrant organ/vocals during the Ice Cream Break. The recording is an audience capture with noticeable balance problems – Jerry’s guitar dominates while Phil’s bass and Bob’s rhythm are often buried, plus a few cuts common to tapes of that period.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews range from 1 to 4 stars; most praise the musical performance while noting significant recording imbalances, yielding an overall average in the low‑mid range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Low volume and uneven mix – Jerry’s guitar is overly loud, Phil’s bass and Bob’s rhythm are muffled; a couple of cuts are present, typical of mid‑60s audience tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑Dead acid‑test vibe with solid playing throughout; occasional disjointed moments but overall a cohesive, high‑energy set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar is excessively forward in the mix yet his surf‑tone runs are praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sounds muffled and gets lost when volume is lowered due to recording balance issues.
band_member_comments.Bob: Shows his early trademark guitar style with nice note‑threading, though often buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pig" McKernan delivers strong organ, vocal, and harmonica work; highlights of the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is present but tends to disappear when the overall volume is reduced.
